**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 05:47
- [EVENT] The Battle of Baltimore took place during the War of 1812, specifically on September 12-14, 1814.
- [EVENT] The bombardment of Fort McHenry by the British Navy was a significant event during the Battle of Baltimore.
- [RELATIONSHIP] Francis Scott Key was an American lawyer and amateur poet.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Francis Scott Key wrote a poem titled "Defence of Fort M'Henry" during the Battle of Baltimore.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "Defence of Fort M'Henry" later became known as "The Star-Spangled Banner," the national anthem of the United States.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Francis Scott Key was aboard a British ship negotiating the release of American prisoners when the bombardment began.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key watched the American flag continue to fly above Fort McHenry despite the intense shelling during the bombardment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key was inspired to write the poem when he saw the flag still waving after the bombardment ceased.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The poem was later set to the tune of a popular British song, "To Anacreon in Heaven."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Star-Spangled Banner" became a popular patriotic song in the United States.
- [TEMPORAL] In 1931, "The Star-Spangled Banner" was officially adopted as the national anthem of the United States.
